headline: Record volumes lift revenue, losses widen, outlook raised
summary_short: Natera's Q1 2026 revenue jumped 38.8% y/y to $696.6M on record test volumes (oncology +54.4%), while the GAAP net loss widened to $85.1M ($0.60/share); management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.74B-$2.82B from $2.62B-$2.70B.
summary_long: Revenue rose 38.8% y/y to $696.6M as processed test volume grew 18.5% (topping 1M units for the first time) and oncology volume grew 54.4%, a record sequential gain. Gross margin expanded to 64.7% from 63.1% on higher ASPs and true-up benefits, though management flagged ~2 points of transient drag from Foresight-related stock comp and a higher receive/report COGS ratio. R&D rose to $210.7M and SG&A to $327.9M, widening the operating loss to $93.5M and the net loss to $85.1M ($0.60/share) from $66.9M a year ago. Cash and investments were $1,087.9M, up $11.8M q/q. Natera raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.74B-$2.82B (from $2.62B-$2.70B) and gross-margin guidance to 64%-66% (from 63%-65%); R&D guidance was also raised to $800M-$900M.

drivers.explanation: Presentation frames Q1 as a record quarter — first time topping 1M processed tests and record sequential oncology unit growth (+24K) — prompting a raised full-year revenue and margin outlook.
Growth attributed to volume acceleration (+18.5% y/y test volume, oncology +54.4%) plus higher ASPs across women's health, organ health and oncology, with continued Signatera ramp.
Margin rose to 64.7% from 63.1% on ASP step-ups and efficient Signatera COGS, partly offset by ~2 points of transient drag from Foresight-related stock comp and a higher receive/report COGS ratio.
Opex rose roughly $148M (+37.5%) y/y to about $538.7M, including R&D of $210.7M and SG&A of $327.9M shown in the financial overview, outpacing the gross-profit gain.
Net loss widened as the ~$148M y/y opex increase (R&D $210.7M, SG&A $327.9M) exceeded the $134.1M y/y gross-profit gain.
Cash & investments rose $11.8M q/q to $1,087.9M, with the UBS line of credit balance unchanged at $80.3M.
